cases.exposure_context_quote: A 52-year-old male farmer presented with complaints of accidental exposure to Dichlorvos while spraying in the field without protection and with the spraying kit strapped to his back.
cases.agent: Dichlorvos (DDVP; 2,2-dichlorovinyl-dimethyl-phosphate), fume exposure during spraying; dose UNVERIFIED
cases.agent_quote: accidental exposure to Dichlorvos while spraying in the field without protection
cases.route: respiratory/cutaneous exposure (fumes) — "exposure to DDVP fumes"; exact primary route UNVERIFIED beyond that
cases.circumstance: accidental exposure while spraying pesticide in the field without protection, spraying kit strapped to his back

symptoms.finding: acute-onset breathlessness requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation for one week
symptoms.quote: Subsequently, he developed acute onset breathlessness for which he was hospitalized and required intubation and mechanical ventilation for one week.
Examination revealed tachycardia (PR-134/min), BP-130/96 mmHg, and normal systemic examination.

symptoms.finding: multifocal consolidation with ground glass opacities on CT-thorax (toxin-mediated allergic pneumonitis)
symptoms.quote: CT-thorax revealed multifocal consolidation with ground glass opacities suggestive of toxin-mediated allergic pneumonitis [Figure 1].
During the second week of hospitalization, the patient developed anuric AKI and required renal replacement therapy (RRT).

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (hospitalized after breathlessness developed; AKI delayed presentation ~1 week after exposure per discussion: 'delayed presentation of AKI after a week of exposure')

labs.name: serum complements, ANCA, ANA
labs.quote: Serum complements, ANCA, and ANA were negative, and creatine-phosphokinase was normal.

labs.name: creatine-phosphokinase
labs.quote: Serum complements, ANCA, and ANA were negative, and creatine-phosphokinase was normal.

labs.name: renal biopsy (first)
labs.value: severe acute tubulointerstitial nephritis (ATIN) with mixed interstitial inflammation; unremarkable glomeruli; EM showed ATN changes
labs.quote: A renal biopsy done during the second week of illness revealed severe acute tubulointerstitial nephritis (ATIN) with mixed interstitial inflammation. Glomeruli were unremarkable [Figure 2a and 2b].

labs.name: creatinine at first discharge
labs.quote: he consequently became dialysis-independent, and creatinine improved to 1.6 mg/dl at discharge [Tables 1 and 2].

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation (1 week)
treatment.quote: he was hospitalized and required intubation and mechanical ventilation for one week.

treatment.name: renal replacement therapy (RRT)
treatment.quote: the patient developed anuric AKI and required renal replacement therapy (RRT).

treatment.name: prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day (first episode)
treatment.quote: He was started on 1 mg/kg/day prednisolone.

treatment.name: IV methylprednisolone followed by 1 mg/kg prednisolone (recurrent episode)
treatment.quote: He was given IV methylprednisolone followed by 1 mg/kg prednisolone, but with no response.

cases.icu_admission: UNVERIFIED (intubation/mechanical ventilation implies critical care, but ICU admission not explicitly stated)
cases.outcome: first episode recovered (dialysis-independent by 4 weeks); recurrent AKI did not respond to steroids; remained dialysis-dependent, progressed to ESRD
cases.sequelae: progression to end-stage renal disease (dialysis-dependent); hospital-acquired infections precluded escalation of immunosuppression
cases.notes: Causality inferred from temporal correlation ('Because of temporal correlation and the absence of any other possibility, ATIN found on renal biopsy was attributed to the exposure to Dichlorvos'); toxin assay unavailable. No cholinergic toxidrome described.
